$comment: INTENDED lifecycle rules for the B2 archive bucket. See
scripts/apply-bucket-lifecycle.mjs for why this is committed and how to
apply or verify it. Changing a number here is a reviewable change;
changing it in the Backblaze console is not, which is the whole point.
THE DAILY TIER IS CAPPED BY A PUBLISHED PROMISE, NOT BY TASTE.
PrivacyPolicy.md (support-tickets section) states that a ticket's backup
copies persist AT MOST 30 DAYS beyond its deletion, and backup.ts keeps
that true by excluding `support_tickets` from the monthly and yearly
tiers so the daily tier is the only place a ticket can be.
For the daily prefixes that makes `daysFromUploadingToHiding` +
`daysFromHidingToDeleting` <= 30 a HARD ceiling. Both terms count: a
version becomes eligible for deletion when it is hidden, and it is
hidden either by the age rule OR by being superseded by a newer upload
at the same key, so the worst-case lifetime is the SUM, not the first
term. An earlier revision set 30 + 30 here, which put the live bucket at
a 60-day worst case and in breach of the published policy.
The split below is a genuine trade-off forced by that ceiling:
- `daysFromUploadingToHiding: 23` is the ordinary restore window, i.e.
how far back the nightly series can be recovered from. Each night
writes a distinct date+nonce key, so in normal operation nothing is
ever superseded and this term alone governs.
- `daysFromHidingToDeleting: 7` is the recovery window for a version
that WAS superseded. That only happens under attack: the Worker's B2
key holds `writeFiles` but not `deleteFiles`, so an attacker can
overwrite an archive but never delete one, and the genuine version
survives as a non-current version for exactly this long. At the
previous value of 1 it was gone before anyone could look, which is
what turned a detectable forgery into an unrecoverable one (#1469).
If a longer forgery-recovery window is wanted, the way to get it is to
exclude `support_tickets` from the DAILY tier as well, which removes the
30-day ceiling entirely. That is a product decision, since it means
tickets have no backup at all, so it is tracked as #1474 rather than
taken here.
The monthly prefixes are NOT capped: tickets are excluded from them, and
the data they do hold (legal-hold audit trail and similar) is exactly
what those tiers exist to keep.
